object_description: two new detached building volumes within an existing school complex
design_condition: The buildings are placed centrally and along the northern plot edge to maximize open space, with access and sports areas arranged across different terrain levels.

positive.statement: The chosen setting generates maximum open spaces.
The northern building’s development layout is interestingly derived from the topography.
The hard court is convincingly framed by the edge of the slope.
The kindergarten building is convincingly organized, with organizational advantages from its connected entrances.
The teaching and group rooms are well proportioned and sufficiently lit.
The covered outdoor spaces provide additional spatial quality.
The setting directly on the district street allows extensive free outdoor play space.

negative.statement: The potential of the outdoor spaces is not exploited, and the parking arrangement is particularly unconvincing.
The buildings form a loose unity and lack spatial cohesion across the complex.
The decentralized arrangement of classrooms and play areas is controversial.
The functional distribution has deficiencies, including missing office provision.
The route from the kindergarten rooms through the cloakrooms to the outdoor play area is somewhat complicated.
The buildings have little in common in appearance, resulting in a lack of overall spatial and functional idea.
